concepts.why: The patient's brain MRI shows marked asymmetry of the cerebral hemispheres, significant atrophy of the right cerebral hemisphere, and areas of cystic encephalomalacia, suggesting a remote focal brain injury, which is consistent with a childhood hemispheric stroke.
The patient has a history of recurrent seizures, which began at age 3 months, and electroencephalography shows focal abnormal brain activity, consistent with epilepsy with focal seizures.
The patient has significant cognitive impairment, marked left hemiparesis with brisk reflexes, and a history of developmental delays, consistent with cerebral palsy, hemiplegic type.
The patient's brain MRI shows areas of cystic encephalomalacia surrounded by gliosis, suggesting a remote focal brain injury, which is consistent with porencephaly.
The patient has a history of recurrent seizures, which began at age 3 months, and electroencephalography shows focal abnormal brain activity, consistent with Rasmussen's encephalitis.
The patient has significant cognitive impairment, marked left hemiparesis with brisk reflexes, and a history of developmental delays, consistent with Sturge-Weber syndrome.
The patient has a history of recurrent seizures, which began at age 3 months, and significant cognitive impairment, consistent with tuberous sclerosis complex.

The patient's brain MRI shows marked asymmetry of the cerebral hemispheres, significant atrophy of the right cerebral hemisphere, and areas of cystic encephalomalacia, suggesting a remote focal brain injury, which is consistent with hemimegalencephaly.
